General Motors Corporation (GM). GM commented that the test procedure for MY 1979 shows an average fuel economy loss of 1.1 mpg or a loss of 6.2 percent. GM stated that the 1979 test procedure results in an increase in the average test horsepower requirements of 5.3 hp or 38 percent. This causes the average fuel economy to decrease by 6.2 percent, and the NOx emissions to increase by an average of 0.23 g/mi.
Chrysler Corporation. Chrysler conducted a series of tests to determine the magnitude of potential emissions and/or fuel economy penalties associated with the "frontal area" method of establishing truck road load horsepower compared to current settings. The tests indicate that the higher "frontal area" horsepower settings will result in significant NOx and composite fuel economy penalties.
